text:
marcy: Heads-up — e2e perf gate failed on main after yesterday's rollout. p95 jumped from ~110ms to ~240ms on the generation workload (test-id: e2e-gen-004). commit abcdef1 -> probably related to last runtime change. CI report: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/4972 :grimacing:

ci-bot: PERF GATE FAILED • e2e-gen-004 • p95 regression +120% • details: https://ci.redwood.example/reports/4972/perf 

samir: ack — looking now. is this from the nightly runner or the canary fleet?

marcy: nightly. canary was green earlier. failure appears in the long-seq traces (seq_len ~1024) only.

jia: I can kick a rerun on that job with trace enabled. Want me to include the kernel and nv driver metadata? :eyes:

marcy: yes please, include host kernel, nv driver, and the quant config. also capture per-stage timings (kv-cache, attention, output).

oliver: possible suspect: my kvcache LRU change landed in abcdef1. If it increases misses for long-seq, p95 could spike. can we bisect between abcde00..abcdef1?

samir: bisect sounds right. but let's rerun first to rule out noise. jia — queue the rerun and then try a fast bisect across the last 5 commits if it reproduces.

jia: rerun queued: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/4978 (started). attaching quick log snippet when it's done.

ci-bot: Build 4978 started by jia. runner: perf-nightly-3. capture-level: verbose.

marcy: thanks. if rerun fails again, oliver can you toggle the kvcache flag (experimental=false) and rerun one job to verify? small patch to gate.

oliver: yea I can push a toggled config to a temp branch and queue. will post PR. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: FYI — infra kernel upgrade rolled to perf-nightly-3 three days ago (kernel 6.1.12 -> 6.2.3). kernel drift noted in infra changelog. Notifying infra team.

samir: good catch. that could also change scheduler behavior for small kernels. once 4978 finishes we should compare stage breakdowns and host metadata.

jia: build 4978 completed — still failing. p95 ~235ms. attached stage timings: KV_CACHE: 28ms, ATTENTION: 152ms, OUTPUT: 44ms. (link: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/4978/stages.json)

marcy: ATTENTION stage jumped a lot. that points to kernel/blas or runtime kernel selection. oliver — please run the kvcache-toggle job anyway so we can rule out both in parallel.

oliver: created PR: https://git.redwood.example/p/redwood/runtime/+/PR-2123 — toggles kvcache LRU. queued test 4982.

ci-bot: Build 4982 queued (branch: PR-2123).

samir: if 4982 is green, kvcache likely culprit. if it fails similarly, lean into infra kernel/driver. either way we should bisect runtime commits between abcde00..abcdef1 for iff. I'm available to run a git bisect tomorrow morning.

marcy: plan set. thank you all. tagging @sre for infra follow-up. I'll create a short postmortem draft if 4982/4983 show clear culprit. :memo:

ci-bot: Build 4982 finished — FAILURE. p95 still ~228ms.

oliver: ok kvcache toggle didn't help. moving to bisect tomorrow. can someone from infra confirm driver/kernel roll history on perf-nightly-3?

sre-bot: infra confirmed kernel 6.2.3 pushed to perf-nightly-3 on 2025-11-02. nv-driver bundle unchanged in that window.

samir: thanks. bisect tomorrow then. leaving notes: - reproduce on perf-nightly-3 - compare ATTENTION kernel timings - bisect runtime commits abcde00..abcdef1 - capture host kernel/driver on each run

marcy: adding a survival checklist in the thread: 1) reproduce (done) 2) fast bisect (scheduled) 3) infra confirm (done) 4) rollback candidate if bisect pinpoints runtime change — likely small config revert 5) postmortem + rollout plan

jia: I'll attach the full perf traces and flamegraphs to the bisect issue once we have the failing commit narrowed down.

marcy: great. closing for now, will post updates from bisect. :wave:
